epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the recap read endpoint
acceptance_criteria: A host or authorized member can read a generated recap for a session through a role-projected response; the response is tenant/workspace/session-scoped and fail-closed; an unauthorized role or foreign tenant gets a hidden-404/403; the participant-facing projection excludes host-only content (T8).
required_tests: Integration: a generated recap is readable by Host/Owner/Admin with the host projection; a participant reading the same recap gets only the participant-safe projection; a foreign-tenant or unknown recap is hidden-404; a non-member is denied; no host-only field leaks into the participant projection.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability/functional - a recap is generated and persisted but has NO HTTP surface, so an end user cannot retrieve it; recorded as a deliberate Core-later deferral in docs/24 CORE-SPEC-003). Domain + role projection already exist: Recap.cs ~32-55 and the recap worker job (CORE-RCP-001/002). Add GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/recap reusing the host-vs-participant projection already exercised by CORE-E2E-003. Authorize like the session read surface; fail-closed; hidden-404. Reuse RecapRepository. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/24 (move recap-read out of deliberately-absent), and the SDK in CORE-SDK-006.

epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the export read and download endpoint
acceptance_criteria: An authorized host/admin can retrieve a completed export artifact through a role-scoped endpoint; the artifact is delivered by a short-lived signed URL or an authorized stream, never a public/static URL (T4/T8); the export projection is role-scoped so a participant-scoped export never contains host-only content; tenant/workspace-scoped; fail-closed; hidden-404.
required_tests: Integration: a completed export is downloadable by Host/Owner/Admin; the download is authorized before any URL/stream is produced; a foreign-tenant or unknown export is hidden-404; a non-authoring role is 403; a participant-scoped export excludes host-only content; an expired or incomplete export is rejected.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability/functional - export is fully modeled, persisted and role-projected under apps/api/Exports but has zero HTTP surface; ExportManifestProjection.cs ~146, ExportJob.cs ~239; recorded deliberately-absent in docs/24 CORE-SPEC-003). New area CORE-EXP. Reuse the export projection + the asset signed-URL pattern (AssetEndpoints.cs ~393-425) - authorize (tenant + workspace membership + role) BEFORE minting any URL; short-lived, private, no public bucket (T4). Add GET /api/v1/exports/{exportId}. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/12, docs/24, and the SDK in CORE-SDK-006.

epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the entity create list and read endpoints
acceptance_criteria: An authoring role can create, list and read generic entities within a workspace; create assigns server-side identifiers and is tenant/workspace-scoped and audited; list/read return only the caller tenant/workspace data with a role-appropriate projection (a participant never receives hidden fields, T2); foreign/unknown entities are hidden-404; non-authoring roles cannot create.
required_tests: Integration: an authoring role creates an entity and reads it back; list returns only same-workspace entities; a foreign-tenant entity is hidden-404; a participant gets the participant-safe projection; a non-authoring role creating is 403; the created entity is audited.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability - a vertical authors its world through generic entities, but EntityEndpoints.cs ~84 currently exposes ONLY MapDelete; create/list/read are deliberately-absent per docs/24 CORE-SPEC-003, which makes the platform unusable for authoring over the API). Reuse the Entity domain/repository and the existing workspace authorization + hidden-404 helpers (mirror SceneEndpoints authoring authz). Generic only - no vertical entity-type logic in Core source (csv/forbidden_core_terms.csv). Add POST, GET list and GET by-id under /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/entities. Fail-closed; hidden-404; audited. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/24, SDK in CORE-SDK-006.

epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the entity-type create list and read endpoints
acceptance_criteria: An authoring role can define, list and read generic entity types within a workspace/tenant; entity-type definitions are stored as data (template key plus field/type metadata), never as hardcoded vertical vocabulary in Core source; tenant/workspace-scoped; audited; foreign/unknown types hidden-404; non-authoring roles cannot create.
required_tests: Integration: an authoring role defines an entity type and lists/reads it; a foreign-tenant type is hidden-404; a non-authoring role is 403; a created type is audited; the boundary scan stays green (no vertical terms).
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability - entity types are how a vertical maps its domain onto Core per the docs/04 template boundary; currently no create/list endpoint, deliberately-absent per docs/24). Store the type as DATA only (docs/04 - no if entityType branching in Core source). Reuse the entity-type model/repository; authorize like entity authoring. Add routes under /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/entity-types. Fail-closed; hidden-404; audited. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/24, SDK in CORE-SDK-006. Pairs with CORE-ENT-006 and CORE-TMPL-001.

epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the template create list and read endpoints
acceptance_criteria: An Owner/Admin can create, list and read template definitions; template content is stored as data (template key plus entity types etc.), never as hardcoded vertical language; an org-scoped lookup never returns a global template for mutation; tenant-scoped; audited; foreign/unknown templates hidden-404; non-privileged roles cannot create.
required_tests: Integration: Owner/Admin creates a template and reads/lists it; a global template is not mutated through the org-scoped route; a foreign-tenant template is hidden-404; a non-privileged role is 403; the boundary scan stays green.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability - TemplateEndpoints.cs ~79 currently exposes ONLY MapDelete and the existing delete row is the only template route in csv/api_routes.csv; create/list deliberately-absent per docs/24). Templates are reusable vertical scaffolding stored as data (docs/04 template boundary). Reuse the Template model/repository + the Owner/Admin authz the delete route already uses. Add POST and GET routes under /api/v1/organizations/{organizationSlug}/templates. Fail-closed; hidden-404; audited. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/24, SDK in CORE-SDK-006.

epic: Vertical Authoring and Read API Completeness
title: Add the content block list and read endpoints
acceptance_criteria: An authoring role can list a scene content blocks and read a single content block with a role-appropriate projection (a participant never receives hidden/unrevealed content, T2); tenant/workspace/scene-scoped; foreign/unknown blocks hidden-404.
required_tests: Integration: an authoring role lists a scene content blocks and reads one back; a participant gets only revealed/visible content via the projection; a foreign-tenant or wrong-scene block is hidden-404; the host vs participant responses differ exactly on the hidden fields.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (consumability - ContentBlockEndpoints.cs ~90-91 exposes only create+delete; there is no list/read, so a client cannot enumerate authored content). Reuse the Content domain + the server-side visibility projection (VisibilityPolicy / the participant visible-feed projection) so reads are filtered server-side, never UI-only (T2). Add GET list /api/v1/scenes/{sceneId}/content-blocks and GET by-id. Fail-closed; hidden-404. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, SDK in CORE-SDK-006.

title: Add stable machine-readable error codes to Problem Details
acceptance_criteria: Every Problem Details response carries a stable machine-readable error code (a type URI or a code extension member) drawn from a documented catalog so a consumer can branch on the code not the human detail string; the three distinct 409s (quota-exceeded, workspace-archived, concurrency-conflict) are distinguishable by code; the code enum is published in @livecore/contracts; no content/PII leaks in the error (T7).
required_tests: Integration: the quota, archived and concurrency 409s return distinct stable codes; a sample of 4xx/5xx responses each carry a code from the catalog; a contract test that the published code enum matches the server catalog.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability - every handler calls Results.Problem(statusCode,title,detail) with NO type and NO extension code (Sessions/SessionEndpoints.cs ~974/983/1015, Persistence/ConcurrencyConflictMiddleware.cs ~62); a grep for type:/extensions: in Results.Problem returns zero; contracts/src/problem-details.ts ~9 declares type? but the server never sets it). Add a shared problem helper that sets a stable code from a documented catalog; publish the enum in @livecore/contracts. Pairs with CORE-RES-001 (the global handler reuses the helper) and CORE-OAS-001. Update docs/08, csv if needed.

title: Expose the optimistic-concurrency token as ETag and honor If-Match
acceptance_criteria: Read responses for mutable aggregates carry the concurrency token as a weak ETag and mutating routes accept If-Match, returning 412/409 on a stale token so a consumer GET-then-PUT across HTTP cannot silently clobber a concurrent change; the existing xmin concurrency tokens are surfaced in the contract DTOs and SDK; an absent If-Match preserves current behavior.
required_tests: Integration: a stale If-Match is rejected (412/409) while a current one succeeds; two clients doing read-modify-write cannot both win; the ETag round-trips through the SDK; existing concurrency tests stay green.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability - the backend paid for xmin concurrency tokens across every mutable aggregate (CORE-CONC-006) but Persistence/ConcurrencyConflictMiddleware.cs only catches an in-request race; the token is never returned (no ETag; SessionResponse etc. carry no version - contracts/src/sessions.ts ~11) and no handler reads If-Match, so a consumer sees last-write-wins). Surface the token as a weak ETag on reads + honor If-Match on mutations. Reuse the existing concurrency token + middleware. Update contracts/SDK (CORE-SDK-006), docs/08. Pairs with CORE-OAS-001.

title: Add bounded pagination to all list endpoints and a session read-one
acceptance_criteria: Every list endpoint (sessions, scenes, workspaces, pending invitations, entities, content-blocks) accepts limit/offset (or a cursor) clamped to a documented maximum with a default and returns a stable items+hasMore envelope like the existing audit page; a new GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId} returns a single role-projected session; no list returns an unbounded array.
required_tests: Integration: a list past the max page size is clamped; hasMore/paging is correct across pages; GET session by-id returns the role-projected session and is hidden-404 for a foreign/unknown id; an over-large workspace does not return an unbounded payload.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability + DoS - only Audit/AuditLogEndpoints paginates (AuditLogPageResponse); every other list returns the full table as a bare array (sessions SessionEndpoints.cs ~220-225, scenes SceneEndpoints.cs ~209-214, workspaces WorkspaceEndpoints.cs ~176-179, pending invitations ~802) and create-scene even loads the whole list to compute next order (SceneEndpoints.cs ~406); there is also no GET session-by-id (scenes have one at SceneEndpoints.cs ~131)). Mirror the AuditLogPageResponse envelope + clamp. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, SDK (CORE-SDK-006). Benefits the CORE-PERF-001 path.

title: Honor Idempotency-Key on create and purchase-verification routes
acceptance_criteria: Unsafe POSTs that create resources or have money/entitlement effects accept an Idempotency-Key and return the original result on replay so a client/network retry cannot double-create or re-run external verification; covered routes include session/scene/content-block/workspace create, asset link create, and the Apple/Google purchase-verification routes; replay is tenant-scoped and bounded by the existing idempotency store.
required_tests: Integration: a repeated create with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original resource and creates exactly one; a retried purchase verify does not re-run the external verifier or re-append audit facts; a different key creates a new resource.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability/correctness - the contract (contracts/src/http.ts ~26) and SDK transport (sdk-ts/src/http.ts ~159) already support Idempotency-Key and an idempotency_keys table + IIdempotencyKeyStore exist, but ONLY the reveal command consumes them; no create handler reads it (CreateSessionAsync SessionEndpoints.cs ~229, CreateSceneAsync SceneEndpoints.cs ~304, CreateContentBlockAsync ContentBlockEndpoints.cs ~97); purchase verify Store/ApplePurchaseEndpoints.cs ~101 dedups only on (provider, transactionId), so a pre-result retry re-runs the verifier and re-appends audit ~164-169/193-198). Reuse IIdempotencyKeyStore. Update docs/08, csv. Pairs with CORE-RES-002.

title: Expose browser-consumer response headers and rate-limit headers
acceptance_criteria: The CORS policy exposes the response headers a browser SDK must read (Retry-After, Location, the request-id header from CORE-OBS-005, and RateLimit-* headers); the rate limiter emits RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset on success and 429; the SDK surfaces retryAfter and rate-limit info on its error type instead of discarding response headers.
required_tests: Integration: a cross-origin response includes the exposed headers; a 429 carries Retry-After + RateLimit-* with no tenant/principal detail (T7); an SDK unit test that the error type exposes retryAfter/rate-limit fields.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (consumability - Hosting/CorsConfiguration.cs ~108-112 sets AllowAnyHeader/Method + AllowCredentials but never WithExposedHeaders (grep zero), so a browser fetch cannot read Retry-After (RateLimitingConfiguration.cs ~251) or Location (SessionEndpoints.cs ~400); no RateLimit-* headers are emitted; the SDK drops all response headers (sdk-ts/src/http.ts ~176, errors.ts ~34)). Add WithExposedHeaders + RateLimit-* + SDK surfacing. Reuse the existing rate limiter + CORS policy. Update docs/08, docs/07, SDK (CORE-SDK-006).

title: Establish an API deprecation and sunset policy
acceptance_criteria: The API has a documented evolution/deprecation policy and the mechanism to honor it - a retiring route or field returns Deprecation and Sunset headers (RFC 8594) with a documented additive-only rule for non-breaking change - so a vertical gets advance signal before a contract changes; the convention is established even if no route is deprecated yet.
required_tests: Integration: a route flagged deprecated returns Deprecation/Sunset headers; a doc/test asserts the additive-only evolution rule; the headers are exposed via CORS (with CORE-DX-005).
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (consumability - versioning is purely the /api/v1 path literal (contracts/src/http.ts ~10); grep for Sunset/Deprecation/api-version returns zero in apps/api; there is no non-breaking evolution path so any change forces a whole v2 cutover with no advance signal). Record the policy in docs/02/docs/23 and add the header mechanism. Pairs with CORE-OAS-001 (the OpenAPI doc marks deprecations). No behavior change beyond the convention.

title: Implement data-subject erasure and anonymization
acceptance_criteria: An authorized request can erase or anonymize a data subject personal data - the user profile (OIDC subject, email, display name), their participant display data, and any invited-email rows - while preserving the PII-free immutable audit chain; erasure cascades/anonymizes via the FKs the schema already defines (export/asset CreatedByUserProfileId ON DELETE SET NULL) so dependent records survive anonymized; the operation is tenant-scoped, authorized, audited by id only, and fail-closed.
required_tests: Integration: after erasure the subject email/display name/OIDC subject are gone or anonymized everywhere they were stored; exports/assets they created survive with a null/anonymized creator; the audit hash chain still verifies; an unauthorized caller is denied.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (privacy/GDPR Art.17 - there is NO erasure path anywhere: IUserProfileRepository exposes only FindByOidcIdentity/Add/Update (no delete/anonymize); UserProfile holds Email+DisplayName (~112-119); Participant.DisplayName and WorkspaceInvitation.InvitedEmail (plaintext) have no erasure. The schema already ASSUMES user deletion - ExportJob.cs ~33/180-181 and Asset CreatedByUserProfileId are NULLABLE ON DELETE SET NULL so the job survives anonymized - but nothing ever deletes a users row. The PII-free audit log (AuditLogEntry holds only ids/enums) makes erasure reconcilable with immutability). Implement the user delete/anonymize command the SET-NULL FKs assume. Update docs/07, docs/10, the privacy doc (CORE-PRIV-005), csv/api_routes.csv.

title: Add authorized tenant organization deletion
acceptance_criteria: An authorized Owner can delete an organization, triggering the existing DB cascade so all that tenant workspaces, sessions, participants, memberships and audit log are removed (tenant offboarding / data deletion); the action is authorized, guarded, and fail-closed; a foreign or unknown organization is hidden-404.
required_tests: Integration: deleting an organization removes all its child data via the cascade; only an authorized Owner may delete (403 otherwise); a foreign-tenant or unknown org is hidden-404; data of other tenants is untouched.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (privacy/offboarding - csv/api_routes.csv has only DELETE .../members/{memberId} and .../templates/{templateId}; there is NO DELETE /api/v1/organizations/{slug}. The cascade config exists but is unreachable: AuditLogConfiguration.cs ~19, OrganizationMemberConfiguration.cs ~80, WorkspaceConfiguration.cs ~107 all OnDelete(Cascade), and OrganizationRepository has no delete). Add the authorized deletion command that triggers the existing cascade (the audit log is intentionally part of tenant teardown). Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, docs/10, the privacy doc.

title: Add configurable data-retention sweeps
acceptance_criteria: A configurable retention policy expires and purges terminal/old personal-data-bearing records - completed/expired sessions and their session events, generated recaps, completed export artifacts (DB row + the S3 object), and closed/expired/revoked invitations (plaintext email) - via worker sweeps; retention windows are configurable with safe defaults and disabled-by-default where deletion would be surprising; purges are audited by id.
required_tests: Integration: a record past its retention window is purged by the sweep (including the export S3 object); a within-window record is retained; disabling a window stops purging; the sweep is idempotent and concurrency-safe.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (privacy/GDPR Art.5(1)(e) + cost - the worker runs only asset-cleanup (pending intents only), recap-gen, export-processing, store-reconciliation; ExportProcessingOptions.cs ~24 and RecapGenerationOptions.cs ~23 explicitly say there is no retention window; SessionEvent/Session/Participant/Recap/completed ExportJob have no ExpiresAt; revoked/accepted invitations are never purged; docs/10 has no retention content; completed exports are never deleted from object storage). Reuse the worker loop + the asset-cleanup pattern + the S3 delete path. Pairs with CORE-RES-002/003 (sweep robustness) and CORE-EXP-001. Update docs/10, docs/13, the privacy doc.

title: Add a data-subject access and portability export
acceptance_criteria: An authorized data subject (or an admin on their behalf) can obtain a machine-readable export of their personal data held by Core (profile, memberships, participant records, invitations) for GDPR Art.15/20 access/portability; this is distinct from the session Exports feature; tenant-scoped, authorized, audited, and PII delivered only to the entitled subject.
required_tests: Integration: a subject retrieves their own personal-data export; another user cannot retrieve it (403); the export contains the documented personal-data set and nothing belonging to other subjects.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (privacy/GDPR Art.15/20 - the only self-service route is MeEndpoints GET / (current principal); no endpoint assembles a subject personal data for access/portability). Reuse the user-profile/membership/participant/invitation repositories. Update csv/api_routes.csv, docs/08, the privacy doc. Pairs with CORE-PRIV-001.

title: Add privacy and data-protection documentation
acceptance_criteria: A privacy/data-protection doc records the PII inventory / data map (what personal data Core stores and where), the controller-vs-processor split for self-hosters, the data-residency configuration (storage and DB region), the default retention windows (CORE-PRIV-003), at-rest encryption expectations, and an explicit consent/legal-basis recording decision - so a self-hoster can assess and configure their compliance posture; doc/csv consistency stays green.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green (CORE-SPEC-001 checks); no Core source change.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (privacy hygiene; docs only - a repo-wide grep for gdpr/privacy/data-subject/residency yields only false positives; Assets__Storage__Region exists (.env.example ~88) but is undocumented as a residency control; DB region is unaddressed; no PII data map exists; the only crypto is SHA-256 hashing of invitation tokens (WorkspaceInvitationToken.cs ~99) - email/display name are plaintext and at-rest encryption is wholly the operator responsibility, undocumented). Mirror the docs/24 decision-register style. Record the consent/legal-basis and field-encryption decisions explicitly (build vs document-as-operator-responsibility). Pairs with CORE-PRIV-001..004.

title: Bound the idempotency-key store with a retention sweep
acceptance_criteria: A configurable worker sweep deletes idempotency_keys rows older than a safe-default window (well beyond any plausible client retry horizon); the sweep is idempotent and concurrency-safe; disabling the window stops purging; deletion is by age only and logged by count, never by key value.
required_tests: Integration: a key past the window is purged and one within it retained; the sweep is a no-op when disabled; concurrent sweeps do not double-delete or error; existing idempotency-replay tests stay green.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (privacy/cost - idempotency_keys rows are inserted on every idempotent create/reveal/purchase replay and are never purged (SystemModule/IdempotencyKeyStore.cs ~43-65 is insert-only; IdempotencyKeyConfiguration.cs has no TTL/expiry column), so the table grows unbounded over a deployment lifetime; the CORE-PRIV-003 retention sweep enumerates session events, recaps, exports and invitations but omits idempotency_keys. Reuse the PRIV-003 worker-sweep and the RES-002/003 lease/dead-letter robustness. Depends on CORE-PRIV-003; pairs with CORE-RES-002/003. Update docs/10, docs/13, the privacy doc (CORE-PRIV-005).

title: Add a global Problem Details exception handler and make realtime delivery best-effort
acceptance_criteria: Every unhandled exception is translated to an RFC 7807 Problem Details response (using the CORE-DX-001 code catalog) instead of a bare framework 500, with no content/PII leak (T7); realtime event delivery is genuinely best-effort - a backplane (Redis/Valkey) send failure is recorded and swallowed so a committed reveal/hide/session/participant operation still returns success instead of 500 during a backplane outage.
required_tests: Integration: an induced unhandled error returns a Problem Details body (not a raw 500); with the backplane unavailable a reveal/hide/start/end and participant join/leave still succeed (state committed, delivery counted-and-dropped); the error response leaks no internal detail.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (resilience - apps/api/Program.cs ~1056-1117 registers the full pipeline but has NO UseExceptionHandler/AddProblemDetails (grep zero); the only translating middleware Persistence/ConcurrencyConflictMiddleware.cs ~50-68 catches only DbUpdateConcurrencyException and rethrows the rest. Compounding it Realtime/SessionEventPublisher.cs ~123-137 DeliverAsync rethrows on any backplane failure and callers await with no try/catch (RevealEndpoints.cs ~364, HideEndpoints.cs ~312, SessionEndpoints.cs ~397/785, join/leave services) - contradicting their own best-effort comments). Add the global handler (reuse the CORE-DX-001 helper) + swallow+count delivery failures. Update docs/02, docs/15.

title: Add worker max-attempt and dead-letter handling
acceptance_criteria: Each worker job carries an attempt counter and transitions to a terminal failed/dead-letter state after a configurable max attempts instead of being retried forever; a permanently-failing low-id item no longer blocks newer work in its batch; ExportJob.Fail() is actually invoked on terminal failure so a broken export surfaces as failed to its requester; dead-lettered items are observable.
required_tests: Integration: a job that fails N times is dead-lettered and stops consuming a batch slot; newer jobs progress past a poison item; a structurally-broken export ends Failed (not Pending forever); the attempt counter increments and is bounded.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (resilience - no attempt counter/poison/dead-letter exists; every reader does Where().OrderBy(Id).Take(batch) (Exports/QueuedExportJobReader.cs ~47-50, Recaps/RecapEligibleSessionReader.cs ~47-48, Store/ReconcilablePurchaseReader.cs ~121-123) so a permanently-failing low-id item is reprocessed every sweep; ExportJob.Fail() exists (Exports/ExportJob.cs ~338-361) but the worker never calls it). Reuse the existing job state machines. Pairs with CORE-RES-003 and CORE-OBS-007 (dead-letter metric). Update docs/15.

title: Add a worker job claim or lease for safe multi-replica processing
acceptance_criteria: Worker job pickup atomically claims/leases each row (e.g. UPDATE ... WHERE status=pending ... SKIP LOCKED RETURNING, or a LockedUntil lease with reclaim) so multiple worker replicas do not redundantly process the same job; a crashed mid-job lease is reclaimable; correctness no longer relies solely on downstream unique constraints; the asset-cleanup row-delete is moved inside the per-item guard so a concurrent-delete race cannot abort the rest of the batch.
required_tests: Integration: two concurrent workers process disjoint job sets (no double-processing); a lease expires and is reclaimed after a simulated crash; a concurrent-delete in asset cleanup does not abort the remaining batch.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (resilience/scale - grep for ClaimAsync/LeaseAsync/LockedUntil/SKIP LOCKED returns zero; every reader is an unguarded Where().OrderBy().Take(); export Start() is in-memory only committed with Complete() (Exports/ExportProcessingService.cs ~204-238) so two replicas both do the full work; the asset-cleanup row-delete is OUTSIDE the per-item try (Assets/ExpiredPendingAssetCleanupService.cs ~147)). The worker is documented horizontally scalable but is not lease-safe. Reuse the existing readers + Postgres SKIP LOCKED. Update docs/13, docs/15.

title: Set database command timeouts and pool sizing
acceptance_criteria: The Npgsql/EF configuration sets a bounded CommandTimeout and a server-side statement_timeout so a stuck query has a ceiling (and retry cannot amplify it unbounded), and the production connection guidance sets a tuned Max Pool Size; the values are configurable with safe defaults; the existing EnableRetryOnFailure execution strategy is preserved.
required_tests: Integration/unit: a query exceeding the command timeout is aborted (not hung); the configured timeout/pool values are applied; existing retry-resilience tests stay green.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (resilience - Persistence/LiveCoreNpgsqlOptions.cs ~62-73 sets only EnableRetryOnFailure(6,30s) and NO CommandTimeout; no statement_timeout/MaxPoolSize/Pooling in the production connection string (deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml ~78/100/136, .env.example ~24-26); a pathological query runs to the Npgsql default and retry can reissue it up to 6 times, risking pool/thread stall). Set CommandTimeout + statement_timeout in LiveCoreNpgsqlOptions.Configure and document MaxPoolSize. Pairs with CORE-PERF-003. Update docs/13, .env.example.

title: Bound outbound dependency calls for storage and OIDC
acceptance_criteria: Outbound calls Core owns have explicit configurable timeouts so a hung dependency fails fast instead of holding a thread - the S3 client has a request Timeout and a bounded retry mode, and the OIDC JwtBearer backchannel has an explicit BackchannelTimeout (and a tuned configuration refresh); defaults are short and safe; storage/auth failures stay fail-closed and contained.
required_tests: Integration/unit: a slow S3 op aborts at the configured timeout; the JwtBearer BackchannelTimeout is applied; an unreachable storage/OIDC dependency fails fast rather than stalling.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (resilience - Assets/AssetStorageServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~84-92 builds AmazonS3Config with only ServiceURL/ForcePathStyle/AuthenticationRegion - no Timeout/MaxErrorRetry/RetryMode, so DeleteObjectAsync (S3CompatibleAssetStorage.cs ~56-71) can block up to the AWS SDK 100s default; IdentityAccess/OidcAuthenticationExtensions.cs ~123-154 sets Authority only - no BackchannelTimeout, so a slow OIDC provider can stall token validation, which with CORE-RES-001 surfaces as a 500). Note Apple/Google verification + notification parsing are deployment-supplied ports (Core makes no outbound HTTP there). Make timeouts configurable. Update docs/12, docs/13, .env.example.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Emit and check in an OpenAPI document for the v1 API
acceptance_criteria: The API produces an OpenAPI 3 document describing every registered /api/v1 route, request/response schema and the Problem Details error shape; the document is generated from the running route table (not hand-maintained), served at a documented endpoint in non-production and emitted as a build artifact; a CI check fails if the committed document does not match the registered routes.
required_tests: A CI/spec test that the generated OpenAPI document covers exactly the routes the minimal API registers (mirrors spec-consistency check 6) and fails on drift; a build test that the document is valid OpenAPI 3.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability/correctness - docs/02 ~72 claims contracts are OpenAPI-derived but apps/api/LiveCore.Api.csproj has NO OpenAPI package and there is no spec; the TS contracts are hand-written and can silently drift from the server). Add Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi (or Swashbuckle) to apps/api; do NOT leak content in schemas (T7) and keep any explorer non-production only. Reuse the route registration + the spec-consistency route enumeration (LiveCoreSpecConsistency.psm1 check 6) to assert coverage. Must run AFTER the new endpoints + error-contract changes (epics 1-4) so the document is complete. Foundation for CORE-OAS-002. Update docs/02, docs/08, README. Justify the new dependency.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Generate the TypeScript contracts from the OpenAPI document with a drift gate
acceptance_criteria: The @livecore/contracts request/response/DTO types are generated from (or validated against) the CORE-OAS-001 OpenAPI document by a repeatable script; a CI gate fails if the committed contracts differ from what the current OpenAPI document produces, so the server and the published types cannot diverge; the generated surface keeps the existing VERSION/lockstep discipline.
required_tests: A CI gate (run in the typescript job) that regenerates the contracts from the OpenAPI document and fails on any diff; the existing contracts type-tests and version-lockstep still pass.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability - eliminates the hand-written contracts drift risk; packages/contracts/src is 833 lines hand-authored today). Use openapi-typescript (or equivalent) wired into the packages/contracts build; keep the public export surface stable (PACKAGE_NAME/VERSION). Reuse the docs/23 versioning rules - a generated breaking change is still a SemVer event in the changelog. Depends on CORE-OAS-001. Update docs/02 (the OpenAPI-derived claim becomes true), docs/23, README. Justify dependencies.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Complete the typed SDK to cover every implemented v1 route
acceptance_criteria: @livecore/sdk-ts exposes a typed client method for every route in csv/api_routes.csv, including the previously-missing me/identity, organizations, audit, templates, entities and entity-types resources and the missing lifecycle methods (participant join/leave, scene reorder/delete/get-by-id, content-block list/read, asset and link deletes, me/entitlements) plus the new phase-6 routes (recap/export read, erasure, tenant deletion, DSAR, session read-one), all typed in terms of @livecore/contracts and routed through the existing fail-closed transport.
required_tests: Per-resource SDK tests for the new methods against a mocked transport asserting method/path/verb/typing; the version-lockstep and build tests stay green.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (consumability - the SDK covers only ~22 of ~49 routes (~45%) today; sdk-ts/src/client.ts plus 9 resource files - whole modules (me, organizations, audit, templates, entities) are absent and a vertical must hand-write fetch for the majority). Reuse the existing resource-client pattern + transport (sdk-ts/src/http.ts). Must run AFTER all route-adding stories (epics 1-4) so it covers them too. Pairs with CORE-SDK-007. Update the package and root CHANGELOG per docs/23.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Complete and drift-gate the TypeScript session-event contract
acceptance_criteria: @livecore/contracts KnownSessionEventTypes equals the non-deferred csv/event_catalog.csv event set (the ten emitted names), each event type has a typed identifier-only payload contract matching the server payload, and a CI gate fails when the TypeScript event vocabulary or payloads diverge from csv/event_catalog.csv and apps/api/Realtime/SessionEventTypes.cs.
required_tests: A contract/drift test that the TypeScript known-event set and payload types match the catalog and fail on a seeded extra/missing/renamed event; a type test that a consumer can discriminate a parsed payload by event type.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability - packages/contracts/src/events.ts ~17 exports KnownSessionEventTypes = ["ContentRevealed"] (1 of 10) while apps/api/Realtime/SessionEventTypes.cs emits ten constants and csv/event_catalog.csv has ten non-deferred rows; packages/contracts/src/realtime.ts ~36 types payload as an opaque string, so a vertical switching on known event names handles 1 of 10 and must blind-parse every payload. Spec-consistency check 11 binds only the C# enum to the catalog, and CORE-OAS-002 generates route DTOs not hub event-type names/payloads, so neither catches this drift). Mirror the check-11 discipline for the TypeScript side. Depends on CORE-OAS-001/002. Update docs/09, docs/23.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Add a typed live realtime client and hub connection contract to the SDK
acceptance_criteria: @livecore/contracts exports the hub path, the SessionEvent client-method name and the connection-parameter shape as stable constants/types, and @livecore/sdk-ts exposes a typed live client that connects, joins only server-managed groups via identifiers (never group names), delivers SessionEventReplayItem-shaped envelopes through one handler shared with reconnect replay, and fails closed without an access token.
required_tests: SDK unit tests asserting the client builds the correct hub URL/params and surfaces a typed event stream; negative tests that a connection without an access token is refused client-side and that a client cannot select a group or another participant's feed.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability - a vertical's primary reason to build on Core is live reveal delivery over the SignalR hub, but the live path exists only as server-side C# constants with no contract mirror or SDK client: RealtimeHubRoutes.cs ~19 (/hubs/session), SessionEventEnvelope.cs ~45 (ClientMethod "SessionEvent"), SessionHub.cs ~18-25 (connection params plus access_token query auth); the SDK RealtimeClient (sdk-ts/src/resources/realtime.ts) covers only REST reconnect-replay, no live connection; no hub constant exists under packages/contracts/src. Reuse the CORE-RT-005 reconnect-replay filtering and the SDK transport. Depends on CORE-SDK-006; the CORE-SDK-007 parity gate must except the hub (it is not a route). Update docs/11, docs/23, README.

epic: Contract Generation and Typed Client Completeness
title: Add a machine-enforced SDK to api-routes coverage parity gate
acceptance_criteria: A CI gate asserts the SDK exposes exactly one typed client method per csv/api_routes.csv route (provider-facing webhook callbacks explicitly excepted), so a future route added without an SDK method, or an SDK method without a route, fails CI - the SDK can never silently fall behind the API again.
required_tests: The gate test itself with seeded drift (a route with no SDK method and an SDK method with no route both fail); runs in the CI typescript job.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability durability - the ~45% SDK coverage regressed silently because nothing enforced parity; mirror the spec-consistency discipline in LiveCoreSpecConsistency.psm1 that binds csv to code). Reuse csv/api_routes.csv as the source of truth. Depends on CORE-SDK-006 being complete (the gate goes green only once coverage is full). Update README and docs/23. No Core source change beyond test/CI tooling.

title: Document the AGPL copyleft model for consumers
acceptance_criteria: A consumer-facing licensing doc states precisely what the Core AGPL-3.0-or-later license means for a vertical app: that importing @livecore/sdk-ts / @livecore/contracts is linking against AGPL code and that deploying the Core API over a network triggers AGPL section 13 for the deployment, and it enumerates which consumption modes are permitted under AGPL vs require a commercial license; a short trademark note clarifies the AGPL grant does not license the LiveCore name.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green; no Core source change.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (consumability clarity; docs only - LICENSE is GNU AGPLv3 (lines 1-2) and SPDX AGPL-3.0-or-later (SystemModule/SourceOffer.cs ~34); docs/16_LICENSING.md and README ~3920-3926 say the Core IS AGPL but never tell a CONSUMING vertical what that means for them; the four packages even carry AGPL-3.0-or-later, so a closed-source importer is by default obligated to release source). Decide and document the permitted consumption modes. Pairs with CORE-LIC-002. Update docs/16, README.

title: Decide and record the commercial or dual-license model
acceptance_criteria: A dated decision records the commercial/dual-licensing model - whether a commercial license is offered (and its terms owner and contact-to-terms path) or the project is explicitly AGPL-only - so a non-AGPL vertical (the named enterprise/closed-commercial case) has a defined legal path or a documented no; the decision notes that a contributor CLA (CORE-LIC-004) is a prerequisite for ever relicensing.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green; no Core source change.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (consumability - README ~3924 and docs/16 ~9/17 only say commercial dual licensing MAY be offered LATER, with no SPDX-expressible alternative grant and no terms; any non-AGPL vertical has NO legal path to use the Core today). Mirror the docs/24 decision-register style. Depends conceptually on CORE-LIC-004 (CLA). Update docs/16, README.

title: Add third-party attribution license files and a CI license gate
acceptance_criteria: The distribution is legally complete and license-checked: a generated third-party NOTICE/attribution inventory for the NuGet + npm runtime dependencies ships in the images and package tarballs, each published package includes the AGPL LICENSE in its files, the Docker images carry OCI org.opencontainers.image.licenses (and source/revision) labels, and a CI license-compliance gate scans the dependency closure/SBOM and fails on a disallowed or unknown license.
required_tests: A build/CI test that the NOTICE exists and is included; that each package tarball contains LICENSE (with CORE-PUB-001); that the image carries the OCI license label; the license gate fails on a seeded disallowed license.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (legal/compliance - no NOTICE/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES/AUTHORS anywhere; the runtime pulls attribution-requiring deps (AWSSDK.S3 Apache-2.0, Npgsql, OpenTelemetry.*, Microsoft.*) and AGPL s7 / Apache s4 require preserving notices on redistribution; packages/*/package.json files=[dist,CHANGELOG.md] omit LICENSE and no per-package LICENSE exists; the Dockerfiles have no OCI license label; CI Trivy (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~524/870) is vuln-only, never license). Reuse the existing SBOM. Pairs with CORE-PUB-001/002. Update .github, deploy, docs/16.

title: Add a contributor IP policy and SPDX source headers
acceptance_criteria: The repo has a contributor IP policy (DCO sign-off or a CLA) with a CONTRIBUTING.md and CI enforcement of sign-off, and first-party source files carry an SPDX-License-Identifier AGPL-3.0-or-later (plus copyright) header enforced by a CI lint - so contribution provenance is clean (preserving the relicensing option needed for CORE-LIC-002) and files retain license context when copied.
required_tests: CI fails a commit without the required sign-off and a shipped source file missing the SPDX header; passes when both are present.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (legal - grep for CLA/DCO/Signed-off-by and SPDX-License-Identifier returns zero; no CONTRIBUTING.md; AGENTS.md has no header policy. Without a CLA/DCO the project cannot guarantee provenance or legally relicense contributions (blocking CORE-LIC-002), and headerless files lose license context on reuse). Add the policy + the SPDX header lint. Update AGENTS.md, .github, README.

title: Pin the AGPL section 13 source offer to the running revision
acceptance_criteria: The GET /source offer resolves to the Corresponding Source of the exact version actually running - the offered URL is pinned to the running revision/tag (e.g. a tree/v<version> or commit-sha URL) rather than the repo root - and the fork-override (SourceOffer:RepositoryUrl) is documented and validated so a modified deployment cannot silently keep offering upstream; the canonical deployment offer always resolves to the corresponding source.
required_tests: Integration: the source offer URL contains the running version/revision; an unset override on a modified build is surfaced/validated per the documented rule; the offer matches the stamped build version.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (legal - SystemModule/SourceOffer.cs ~59-66 returns {license,version,sourceUrl} where sourceUrl defaults to the repo root and is not pinned to the exact tag/revision, so a remote user cannot reliably fetch the exact running source (AGPL s13 requires Corresponding Source of the running version); nothing validates a fork set RepositoryUrl). Derive a revision-pinned URL from the stamped build version. Reuse ResolveBuildVersion(). Update docs/16.

title: Make the four packages publishable
acceptance_criteria: @livecore/contracts, @livecore/sdk-ts, @livecore/ui-core and @livecore/design-tokens are no longer private and each declares a correct published surface (files/exports/main/module/types incl. the LICENSE file, publishConfig with access and registry, repository/license/sideEffects), so pnpm pack produces a complete importable tarball for each; nothing internal/test/source-only leaks into the package; the lockstep VERSION discipline is unchanged.
required_tests: A package-build test per package asserting the packed tarball (pnpm pack --json) contains the declared entry points + types + CHANGELOG + LICENSE and excludes tests and non-shipping sources; version-lockstep stays green.
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (consumability - ALL FOUR packages are private:true (packages/*/package.json line 4) with no publishConfig, so a vertical in another repo CANNOT install them; the only path today is workspace:* inside this monorepo; docs/23 ~132-135 records publishing as a follow-up). Remove private; add publishConfig and choose the registry (GitHub Packages or npm) and record the decision in docs/23; include LICENSE in files (with CORE-LIC-003). Keep workspace:* dev links working. Does not yet wire the CI publish (CORE-PUB-002). Update docs/23, README. Pairs with CORE-PUB-002/003.

title: Wire the release-gated package publish pipeline
acceptance_criteria: On a release tag the CI publish job builds and publishes all four packages to the chosen registry at the shared lockstep version, gated by the existing release-version gate (scripts/assert-release-version.ps1) and version-lockstep so a mismatched or un-lockstepped version cannot publish; every push/PR runs a publish dry-run (pnpm pack / --dry-run) proving the pipeline without pushing; a republish of an existing version is refused (immutability).
required_tests: scripts/test-release-version.ps1 still passes; a dry-run job that packs all four packages on every PR; the gate refuses a version that disagrees with the release tag or is out of lockstep (fail-closed).
notes: TIER 1 BLOCKER (consumability - the CI publish job today pushes Docker images only; there is no npm publish anywhere - .github/workflows/ci.yml publish ~773). Reuse the existing release-version + lockstep gates (docs/23 - the same shared-version invariant) and the immutable-tag posture. Depends on CORE-PUB-001. Add npm auth via a CI secret (no secret in repo). Update docs/23, README, .github. Justify any new tooling.

title: Document consumption and add a minimal worked consumer example
acceptance_criteria: A documented quick start shows a vertical app installing the published packages from the registry, authenticating, constructing the SDK client (logging PACKAGE_NAME/VERSION) and calling the API; a minimal example consumer in the repo compiles against the published-shape packages and is built in CI, giving vertical authors a reference integration that did not exist before.
required_tests: CI builds the example consumer against the package public surfaces (not internal source) so a breaking change to the published surface fails the example build.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (consumability/adoption - there is no reference web app and no worked SDK integration anywhere; apps/ is api+worker only, so a vertical author has zero starting point). Keep the example product-neutral (the boundary scan applies) - no ArcanOS/Enterprise terms. Depends on CORE-PUB-001 (published shapes) and benefits from CORE-SDK-006 and CORE-DEP-006 (a local OIDC+API to talk to). Update README, docs/02, docs/23. Do NOT create product UI screens - keep it a minimal client/integration sample. Justify dependencies.

title: Publish the npm packages with build provenance and complete the publish-shape
acceptance_criteria: The release publish runs the package publish with npm build provenance (--provenance or publishConfig.provenance) under a scoped id-token write permission, so each published @livecore/* version carries a verified provenance attestation; every package.json declares engines (the supported Node range) and repository.directory pointing at packages/<name>.
required_tests: The publish dry-run asserts each packed manifest carries engines and repository.directory; a release-time check (or documented verification step) confirms the provenance statement is attached to each published version.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (consumability/supply-chain - CORE-PUB-002 wires npm publish but its acceptance lists only registry/version-gate/immutability, not provenance or id-token; CORE-PUB-001 publish-shape omits engines and repository.directory (packages/contracts/package.json ~1-21 has none). npm provenance is the npm-side analogue of image attestation (CORE-SEC-008) and the lowest-cost way to make the @livecore/* tarballs verifiably built by this pipeline). No new dependency (npm-native --provenance). Depends on CORE-PUB-001/002; pairs with CORE-SEC-008. Update docs/23, README.

title: Make the audit log tamper-proof in code not only tamper-evident
acceptance_criteria: The audit log cannot be mutated from inside the running process - audit read paths return non-tracked entities, a persistence interceptor blocks any UPDATE/DELETE targeting audit_logs and throws fail-closed, and a checked-in migration REVOKEs UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs from the runtime application role; the existing append + per-tenant hash chain (CORE-SEC-003) and the verifier keep working.
required_tests: A read of an audit entry followed by SaveChanges does NOT persist a mutation (the interceptor blocks it); an attempted UPDATE/DELETE on audit_logs throws; the migration is asserted to issue the REVOKE; the hash-chain verifier still verifies a clean chain and still detects a tampered one.
notes: TIER 1 HIGH (security - the chain is tamper-EVIDENT but not tamper-PROOF out of the box: AuditLogRepository.cs ListByOrganizationAsync ~112, ListPageByOrganizationAsync ~138 and ListChainByOrganizationAsync ~178 omit AsNoTracking (the internal reads at ~79/~104 use it), and the REVOKE is operator-documentation-only - Program.cs ~558 defers it). Add AsNoTracking to the three reads, a SaveChanges/Db interceptor denying writes to audit_logs, and a migration that REVOKEs UPDATE/DELETE for the runtime role. Reuse AuditLogChain.cs ~67-176 + AuditLogChainVerifier. Pairs with CORE-CONC-008. Update docs/07, docs/13, and csv/migration_destructive_down_review.csv if relevant.

title: Wrap the non-transactional audit appends in a unit of work
acceptance_criteria: Every audit append happens inside a transactional unit of work so the per-tenant sequence-counter lock is held until the insert commits and concurrent same-tenant appends cannot fork or reorder the hash chain; the previously direct (non-ambient-transaction) appends are brought under the CORE-CONC-002 transaction semantics.
required_tests: A concurrency test: many concurrent same-tenant audited actions produce a single unbroken, gap-free hash chain (no fork, no false-positive tamper detection); the existing audit tests stay green.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (security/integrity - AuditLogRepository.AppendAsync ~40-53 is only atomic inside TransactionalUnitOfWork, but Organizations/OrganizationEndpoints.cs ~331 and Visibility/RevealService.cs ~325 append without an ambient transaction, so the sequence lock releases before commit and concurrent appends can fork the chain - which the verifier later reports as tampering, a false positive masking real detection). Reuse the existing TransactionalUnitOfWork (CORE-CONC-002). Pairs with CORE-SEC-004. Update docs/07 if needed.

title: Add configurable HSTS and HTTPS redirection
acceptance_criteria: The API can enforce HSTS and HTTPS redirection via configuration; defaults are documented for the TLS-terminating reverse-proxy posture (forwarded headers already trusted), so a deployment that is not behind a terminating proxy still gets an app-level Strict-Transport-Security header and redirect; all toggles are configurable and disabled only where the documented proxy terminates TLS.
required_tests: Integration: with HSTS enabled the response carries Strict-Transport-Security; with redirection enabled an HTTP request is redirected; with the proxy posture configured the behavior matches the documented default; no regression to forwarded-headers handling.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (security - there is no UseHttpsRedirection or UseHsts anywhere in apps/api (confirmed); TLS/HSTS is entirely delegated to an edge the app cannot verify exists). Reuse the existing ForwardedHeadersConfiguration. Add UseHsts/UseHttpsRedirection guarded by config so the proxy case is unchanged but standalone is protected. Update docs/07, docs/13, .env.example.

title: Close the rate-limiting gaps on anonymous surfaces
acceptance_criteria: The anonymous SignalR negotiate and other anonymous non-webhook surfaces are covered by a per-IP rate limit, and the anonymous store-notification webhook retains a non-disableable request-rate floor (the body-size cap already survives) so disabling the global limiter cannot fully remove webhook volume protection; all limits stay configurable and 429 Problem Details leak no tenant/principal detail (T7/T9).
required_tests: Integration: flooding the SignalR negotiate is throttled with 429; with the global limiter disabled the webhook still enforces a floor; 429 responses carry no tenant/principal/resource detail; the existing rate-limit tests stay green.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (security/DoS - RateLimitingConfiguration.cs ~159-187 makes both limiters no-op when Enabled=false (the body-size cap survives), and anonymous non-webhook surfaces including the /hubs/session negotiate have no in-app limit ~163-169). Reuse the existing fixed-window per-IP policy + the StoreNotificationEndpoints body-size cap pattern. Keep configurability but add a floor. Update docs/07, .env.example.

title: Add an asset content-type allowlist and absolute size ceiling
acceptance_criteria: Asset upload-intent validates content-type against a configurable MIME allowlist and enforces a configurable absolute per-object size ceiling independent of the workspace quota; a disallowed type or oversize object is rejected fail-closed before any signed upload URL is minted; the privacy model (private buckets, signed URL after authorization) is unchanged.
required_tests: Integration: a disallowed content-type is rejected; an over-ceiling object is rejected before a URL is minted; an allowed in-limit upload still succeeds; the rejection leaks no storage detail.
notes: TIER 3 LOW (hardening - Assets/Asset.cs ~455-456 treats content-type as a free-form token with no MIME allowlist and there is no absolute per-object ceiling beyond the workspace quota; neither breaks privacy but both are abuse surfaces). Reuse the existing upload-intent path + the AssetDownloadPolicy fail-closed posture. Make the allowlist/ceiling configurable. Update docs/12, .env.example.

title: Add baseline HTTP security response headers
acceptance_criteria: A configurable middleware adds to every API, error and SignalR-negotiate response X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and a deny-all Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'), defensible because the API returns only JSON/Problem-Details and never renders HTML; headers are on by default and individually configurable and leak no tenant/principal detail (T7).
required_tests: Integration: an authenticated JSON response and a Problem-Details error response both carry nosniff plus Referrer-Policy plus the CSP; 404/406/500 paths still carry them; toggling a header off via config removes exactly that header; no PII in any header.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (security - CORE-SEC-005 adds only HSTS plus HTTPS-redirect; a grep for X-Content-Type-Options/Content-Security-Policy/Referrer-Policy/frame-ancestors across apps/api returns zero (Program.cs ~1056-1117 registers the pipeline with no header middleware; only Kestrel AddServerHeader=false is set), so JSON/error responses are served with no anti-sniffing or framing defense). Add a small configurable response-header middleware. Conservative scope: a deny-all CSP because the API renders no HTML, no script/style sources, no separate X-Frame-Options (subsumed by frame-ancestors). Complements CORE-SEC-005. Update docs/07, .env.example.

title: Bind the declared content-length and content-type into the signed asset upload URL
acceptance_criteria: The presigned upload URL pins the declared Content-Type and constrains object size to the declared/ceiling value (a SigV4 content-length-range / Content-Type signed condition, or an equivalent fail-closed post-upload size/type reconciliation on confirm that releases the reserved quota); an upload whose actual bytes or type violate the signed constraints is rejected by storage or never confirmed, and the rejection leaks no storage coordinate.
required_tests: Negative: a URL minted for image/png and N bytes rejects (or leaves unconfirmed, fail-closed) an upload of a different content-type or of more than N bytes, and the reserved quota is released; an in-spec upload still succeeds; no storage detail leaks on rejection.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (security/quota-bypass - CORE-AST-007 validates the client-declared contentType/sizeBytes BEFORE minting the URL and the intent reserves sizeBytes against the storage quota (CORE-MON-006), but the minted presigned PUT binds only bucket/key/verb/expiry (Assets/S3CompatibleAssetStorage.cs ~87-93 builds GetPreSignedUrlRequest with no ContentType or content-length-range), so a client can declare 1 byte / an allowed MIME then PUT a multi-gigabyte object of any type, bypassing both the workspace quota and the AST-007 ceiling/allowlist, which only ever see the declared metadata). Keep the private-bucket/signed-URL privacy model unchanged. Depends on CORE-AST-007. Update docs/12.

title: Enforce high-value domain invariants as database CHECK constraints
acceptance_criteria: Additive (expand-only) migrations add CHECK constraints for the high-value invariants the aggregates already enforce (status-enum ranges, scene_order >= 0, revision_number >= 1, non-negative quota_usage and asset byte counters, sequence >= 1); valid writes are unaffected and an out-of-range value is rejected at the database.
required_tests: Integration (Postgres): a raw INSERT/UPDATE with an out-of-range enum or a negative order/usage is rejected by the constraint; every existing test stays green; the destructive-down review (csv/migration_destructive_down_review.csv) is unaffected since the migrations add, not drop.
notes: TIER 3 LOW (defense in depth - a grep for HasCheckConstraint across apps/ returns zero; invariants live only in aggregate guards (e.g. Realtime/SessionEvent.cs ~121-126; quota math in Entitlements/QuotaEnforcementService.cs), so a direct DB write (the migration/owner role legitimately retains DELETE for teardown), a future raw-SQL path or a mapping regression can persist a code-impossible state - the same tamper-resistance posture CORE-SEC-004 pursues for the audit log. Additive and behavior-neutral. Does NOT add the deliberately-absent polymorphic FKs (CORE-SPEC-003 register). Pairs with CORE-SEC-004. Update docs/10.

title: Collapse the audience reveal fan-out to a single rule lookup and shared group
acceptance_criteria: An audience-wide reveal resolves recipients with a single visibility-rule lookup and an in-memory gate over the participant set (not one visibility_rules query per participant) and delivers via a shared session-audience SignalR group (one backplane publish) rather than one publish per participant; per-participant lookups/groups are reserved for selected-participant events; reveal latency and DB/backplane load no longer grow linearly with audience size; visibility correctness is unchanged.
required_tests: Integration: an audience reveal to many participants issues one rule lookup and one audience-group send (asserted), not N; selected-participant reveals still go only to the entitled participants; a performance assertion that per-reveal query count is independent of audience size; existing visibility/realtime correctness tests stay green.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (scale - Realtime/SessionEventRecipientResolver.cs ~137-150 loops every active participant calling CanParticipantReceiveAsync -> VisibilityPolicy -> VisibilityRuleRepository.ListByResourceAsync (Visibility/VisibilityRuleRepository.cs ~126) = 1+N identical queries per event (a Scene reveal emits two events -> 2x(1+N)), all awaited inside the host HTTP request (RevealEndpoints.cs ~362-365); plus SessionEventPublisher.DeliverAsync ~121-127 does a separate per-participant SendToGroupAsync = N backplane publishes). The 25-participant full-house test hides the linear blow-up. Reuse VisibilityPolicy (in-memory gate) + add a shared audience group. Preserve fail-closed visibility. Update docs/11.

title: Make reconnect replay bounded and cursored
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect replay reads only events after the client cursor with a SQL-side WHERE sequence greater-than cursor and a row cap (not the whole stream loaded then filtered in memory) and resolves recipient visibility for the replayed slice in batch (reusing CORE-PERF-001) so replay cost is bounded and does not grow with events times participants; replay correctness/filtering is unchanged.
required_tests: Integration: replay loads only post-cursor rows up to the cap (asserted query), not the full stream; a long well-attended session reconnect issues a bounded query count; replayed events are still correctly visibility-filtered.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (scale/DoS - Realtime/SessionReplayService.cs ~113-140 loads the ENTIRE stream (SessionEventRepository.ListBySessionAsync, Realtime/SessionEventRepository.cs ~93 - no sequence-greater-than-cursor filter, no limit) then calls ResolveAsync per event (itself the PERF-001 fan-out); a reconnect storm becomes a self-inflicted DoS). Push the afterSequence cursor + cap into SQL; batch-resolve. Depends on CORE-PERF-001. Update docs/11.

title: Enable DbContext pooling and cache per-request authz lookups
acceptance_criteria: The API/worker register the DbContext with pooling (AddDbContextPool) and the stable per-request authorization lookups (organization-by-slug, user-profile-by-OIDC, membership/role) are served from a short-TTL cache invalidated on membership change, so a high request rate does not re-issue the same authz queries and re-allocate a DbContext on every request and hub connect; correctness/fail-closed authz is unchanged.
required_tests: Integration: repeated requests by the same principal do not re-issue the org/profile/membership queries within the TTL (asserted); a membership change invalidates the cache; authz decisions are unchanged (foreign/role denials still fail-closed).
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (scale - registration uses AddDbContext not AddDbContextPool (Program.cs ~270 + worker extensions); every authenticated request runs TenantContextResolver.ResolveAsync = 3 sequential queries before the endpoint, plus per-endpoint membership re-queries (e.g. two HasRoleAsync in Visibility/VisibilityEndpoints.cs ~308-330); no IMemoryCache/IDistributedCache/HybridCache anywhere). Add pooling + a short-TTL authz cache with explicit invalidation. Pairs with CORE-RES-004. Update docs/02, docs/15.

title: Compute the visible-feed in memory and add the documented visibility index
acceptance_criteria: GET /participants/{id}/visible-feed computes the participant visible set in memory from a single workspace-rule load (plus a session filter) instead of one policy query per candidate resource, and the visibility_rules (workspace_id, resource_type, resource_id) index the cleanup path documents is actually created (or the delete is rescoped to an existing index); feed correctness is unchanged.
required_tests: Integration: the visible-feed endpoint issues a bounded query count independent of resource volume (asserted); the feed contents are unchanged vs the previous per-candidate computation; the new index exists (migration asserted).
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (scale - Visibility/VisibilityPreviewService.cs ~128-158 calls ListByWorkspaceAsync then for each candidate calls CanParticipantViewResourceAsync -> another ListByResourceAsync, re-fetching rows it already holds (1+M queries); and VisibilityRuleRepository.RemoveByResourceAsync ~226-231 filters on (Org,Workspace,ResourceType,ResourceId) but the snapshot has only (Org,Workspace) and (Session,ResourceType,ResourceId) - the documented (workspace_id,resource_type,resource_id) index does not exist). Reuse the single workspace-rule load. Add the index migration. Update docs/10, docs/11.

title: Stream the audit-chain verification
acceptance_criteria: Audit hash-chain verification reads the chain in ordered segments via an (organization_id, sequence) cursor instead of materializing a tenant entire chain in memory, so verification memory/time stay bounded as the audit log grows; detection of a tampered/broken/reordered chain is unchanged.
required_tests: Unit/integration: chain verification over a large chain runs in bounded memory (segmented reads asserted); a clean chain verifies and a tampered one is still detected at the first broken entry.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (scale - Audit/AuditLogRepository.cs ListChainByOrganizationAsync ~178-199 loads a tenant ENTIRE chain into memory with no bound/streaming (ListByOrganizationAsync ~112 is also unbounded but appears unused; the audit endpoint correctly uses the paged variant). Segment the verification by the existing (organization_id, sequence) order. Reuse AuditLogChainVerifier. Pairs with CORE-SEC-004 and CORE-PERF-003. Update docs/07.

title: Add HTTP response compression for JSON
acceptance_criteria: The API compresses JSON responses (Brotli/Gzip) via response-compression middleware for list/feed/replay payloads, excluding the realtime hub transport and already-compressed content; compression is configurable; no change to response contents.
required_tests: Integration: a large JSON list response is returned compressed when the client accepts it; the SignalR hub transport is not double-compressed; small/streaming responses behave correctly.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (scale/bandwidth - no UseResponseCompression/AddResponseCompression anywhere; the pipeline (Program.cs ~1056-1117) has none, and replay/feed/list responses are JSON arrays that can be large, inflating bandwidth/latency for large sessions and mobile clients). Add response compression excluding the hub. Update docs/02.

title: Index the tenant audit-log page read
acceptance_criteria: The audit-log page read is backed by an index that satisfies its WHERE organization_id ... ORDER BY ordering (add an (organization_id, id) index, or re-point the paged read at the already-indexed (organization_id, sequence) append order); the model snapshot asserts the index exists and the paged read's ORDER BY column is index-covered, so paging does not full-sort a tenant's unbounded audit prefix.
required_tests: A migration/snapshot test asserting the chosen covering index exists; an integration test over a large seeded tenant log asserting correct pages and an index-backed ordering (no full sort) independent of offset depth.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (scale - Audit/AuditLogRepository.cs ~168-174 ListPageByOrganizationAsync does Where(OrganizationId==org).OrderBy(Id).Skip/Take, reached live by AuditLogEndpoints.cs ~147; the only declared audit_logs indexes are (organization_id, created_at) and (organization_id, sequence) (LiveCoreDbContextModelSnapshot.cs ~231-236) - neither satisfies an id-ordered read, so Postgres sorts the matched prefix on every page. Every workspace-scoped id-ordered list has a (workspace_id, id) index; audit is the one organization-scoped id-ordered list without a matching composite. Complements CORE-DX-003; CORE-PERF-005 already orders by the indexed sequence so it is unaffected. Update docs/10.

title: Compute audience-filtered entity search in memory from a single rule load
acceptance_criteria: The audience-participant entity-search path issues a query count independent of entity volume (one workspace-rule load plus the entity load, gated in memory) with filtering results unchanged versus the per-candidate computation, reusing the CORE-PERF-004 in-memory visibility gate so the visible-feed and entity-search paths cannot diverge.
required_tests: A query-count assertion that an audience search over N entities issues O(1) rule queries (not O(N)); equivalence tests that the visible set matches the current per-candidate result for audience-wide, selected-participant, cross-session and host cases.
notes: TIER 3 LOW (scale, latent - Entities/EntitySearchService.cs ~212-229 loops candidates calling _policy.CanParticipantViewResourceAsync per entity, each issuing its own VisibilityRuleRepository.ListByResourceAsync (VisibilityPolicy.cs ~245 -> VisibilityRuleRepository.cs ~126) = the identical 1+M fan-out CORE-PERF-004 fixes for the visible-feed, in a path PERF-004 does not name. Latent today (no HTTP endpoint, deliberately-absent per CORE-SPEC-003) but CORE-ENT-006 (entity list/read) moves the audience-filter pattern toward a live path. Depends on CORE-PERF-004 (reuse its gate); relates to CORE-ENT-006. Update docs/11.

title: Add distributed tracing auto-instrumentation and a correlation-id response header
acceptance_criteria: OpenTelemetry tracing includes ASP.NET Core, HttpClient and EF Core auto-instrumentation so DB queries, outbound HTTP and framework operations nest as child spans under the request span (exported via the existing OTLP exporter), and the request/trace id is returned to the caller in a response header (e.g. X-Request-Id / W3C traceparent) and present in every log line, so a consumer can correlate a failed call with server traces/logs; inbound traceparent is propagated.
required_tests: Integration: a request trace contains child spans for a DB call and an outbound HTTP call; the response carries the request/trace id header; the id appears in the request log scope; inbound traceparent is honored.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (observability - LiveCore.Api.csproj ~50-89 references OTel hosting + Prometheus + OTLP exporters but NO Instrumentation.AspNetCore/.Http/.EntityFrameworkCore; TracingServiceCollectionExtensions.cs ~83 only AddSource(LiveCore), so the trace has just 3 hand-rolled spans (LiveCoreActivitySource.cs ~50-76) - DB/S3/OIDC/SignalR are invisible. RequestLogContextMiddleware.cs ~65 uses TraceIdentifier as request_id in logs but nothing echoes it back (grep for a response X-Request-Id/traceparent is zero)). Add the instrumentation packages + a response-header middleware. Reuse the existing OTLP exporter. Update docs/15. Justify the new dependencies.

title: Enforce log redaction as a guardrail not a convention
acceptance_criteria: ID-only structured logging (T7) is enforced mechanically - either via a compliance redaction layer or a Roslyn analyzer/test that fails the build on a log template that interpolates content/PII/token values - so a future content-bearing log statement cannot ship; existing ID-only logs are unaffected.
required_tests: The guardrail fails on a seeded content-bearing/interpolated log template and passes on the existing ID-only logs.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (security/privacy - no Microsoft.Extensions.Compliance.Redaction, [DataClassification]/[LogProperties], or any scrub layer exists (grep zero); T7 ID-only logging is reviewer-discipline only (current logs e.g. StoreNotificationReconciliationService.cs ~135-149, ExportProcessingService.cs ~155 are correctly ID-only, so no active leak). Add an enforced guardrail. Update docs/07, docs/15.

title: Add SLI metrics for auth failures rate-limit rejections and worker jobs
acceptance_criteria: Metrics cover the key service-level indicators - authentication/authorization failure (401/403) rate, rate-limit (429) rejections, and per-loop worker job success count, duration histogram and backlog/queue depth - in addition to the existing instruments, so an operator can alert on an auth-failure spike, a rate-limit storm, or a worker falling behind; no PII in metric labels (T7).
required_tests: Integration: a 401/403 increments the auth-failure metric; a 429 increments the rate-limit metric; a worker loop records success/duration and a backlog gauge; labels carry no tenant/principal detail.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (observability - LiveCoreMetrics.cs ~53-60 defines 8 instruments; the error counter (~151) increments only on 5xx (401/403 counted nowhere); no rate-limit-rejection counter (the 429 path records none); the worker records only job.failures (~127) - no success count, duration histogram, or backlog depth for the four loops, so a queue can back up with green metrics). Reuse the existing meter. Pairs with CORE-OBS-008 and CORE-RES-002. Update docs/15.

title: Ship example alert rules SLOs and a starter dashboard
acceptance_criteria: The repo ships example Prometheus alert/recording rules, documented SLO targets for the livecore_* series, and a starter Grafana dashboard, plus scrape guidance, so a self-hoster gets actionable alerting/observability out of the box instead of raw metrics with no thresholds.
required_tests: The alert rules/dashboard are validated (e.g. promtool check rules / JSON lint) in CI; doc references stay consistent.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability - deploy/ has only compose/ (docker-compose.yml, .env.example, README); no Prometheus scrape_config, alert/recording rules, or Grafana dashboard; docs/13 ~80/493-497 only says /metrics exists and should be scraped, with no what-to-alert-on guidance or SLO targets). Build on the CORE-OBS-007 metrics. Update docs/15, deploy/, README.

title: Add deep readiness checks for OIDC storage and the backplane
acceptance_criteria: /health/ready performs live reachability checks (tagged ready) for the OIDC discovery endpoint, the object-storage backend and the realtime backplane, in addition to the existing DB check, so a host with a valid DB but a dead critical dependency leaves the rotation instead of reporting Ready; liveness stays shallow/separate; checks are bounded by short timeouts (CORE-RES-005) and fail-closed.
required_tests: Integration: readiness reports Unhealthy when OIDC/storage/backplane is unreachable and Healthy when all are up; liveness is unaffected; the checks honor short timeouts.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability - API readiness registers only AddDbContextCheck (Program.cs ~996-997) plus RequiredDependencyHealthCheck, which is a startup-captured boolean of config presence (Hosting/RequiredDependencyReadiness.cs ~49-53/96-108), not a live probe; OIDC/storage/backplane reachability is never checked, so a host with a dead dependency reports Ready and takes traffic). Reuse the health-check infra; tag ready vs live. Pairs with CORE-RES-005 (timeouts). Update docs/13, docs/15.

title: Gate readiness on the database schema being up to date
acceptance_criteria: In a configured-persistence host /health/ready reports not-ready (503, tagged ready) when GetPendingMigrationsAsync returns any migration the build expects but the database lacks, and ready once the schema is current; /health/live stays shallow and unaffected; the check is bounded by a short timeout (CORE-RES-004/005) and leaks no schema detail.
required_tests: Integration: apply all-but-the-last migration, start the API, assert /health/ready is 503 and /health/live 200; apply the last migration, assert readiness flips to ready.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability/deploy-safety - readiness registers only AddDbContextCheck (a connectivity probe, Program.cs ~996-997) plus the startup-captured config-presence RequiredDependencyHealthCheck (Hosting/RequiredDependencyReadiness.cs ~49-53); GetPendingMigrationsAsync is never called, so if the migrate step is skipped/failed or the API image is rolled forward ahead of its schema the API reports ready and 500s at first query instead of leaving rotation. Distinct from CORE-OBS-009 (dependency reachability) - this is schema-version readiness. Reuse the health-check infra; tag ready vs live. Depends on CORE-RES-004/005; pairs with CORE-OBS-009. Update docs/13, docs/15.

title: Make log level and format an operator configuration surface and document it
acceptance_criteria: The .env.example and the docs/13 self-hosting configuration contract list the log-level env var(s) (e.g. Logging__LogLevel__Default and a per-category override) and the format posture (the JSON console formatter) with safe defaults; setting Logging__LogLevel__Default=Debug demonstrably changes emitted verbosity; the doc/CSV consistency checks stay green.
required_tests: Integration/host test that overriding Logging__LogLevel__Default via environment changes the host's minimum emitted level; a doc review that every documented logging env key resolves in the host.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability - docs/13 ~13 names "logging level" as required runtime configuration, but the operator contract (.env.example, the CORE-OPS-008 table in docs/13) never lists Logging__LogLevel__Default or a format control; apps/api/appsettings.json ~36-41 and apps/worker/appsettings.json hard-code the LogLevel block, so a self-hoster has no documented way to raise/lower production verbosity. Distinct from CORE-OBS-005 (correlation header) and CORE-OBS-006 (redaction). Standard .NET config key plus contract docs. Update .env.example, docs/13, README.

title: Add CodeQL static analysis to CI
acceptance_criteria: CodeQL (or an equivalent SAST) analyzes both the C# and the TypeScript sources on every push/PR and the build fails on a high/critical finding; the gate is wired into the same required-checks set the publish job depends on, so first-party code is statically security-analyzed for the first time.
required_tests: The CodeQL workflow runs on PR and reports; a seeded or known issue path proves it fails closed on a high/critical finding (or the chosen severity gate is documented).
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (security/supply-chain - CI has NO SAST/CodeQL today; first-party code is never statically analyzed - container images are Trivy-scanned and lockfiles pinned, but that is dependencies not code). Add a codeql job for csharp + javascript-typescript in .github/workflows. Reuse the existing required-checks gating (publish needs all jobs). Update docs/14, the README CI section.

title: Add a dependency vulnerability audit gate
acceptance_criteria: CI fails on a known-vulnerable first-party dependency - dotnet list package --vulnerable (transitive included) for the .NET projects and pnpm audit (or Dependabot with a blocking policy) for the workspace - at an agreed severity; the existing PR image CVE scan is promoted to blocking on critical (today it is report-only on PRs, blocking only on a release).
required_tests: The audit job runs on PR; a seeded vulnerable-package fixture (or a documented policy test) proves it fails closed; the image-scan gate logic test (scripts/test-image-scan.ps1) still passes.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (supply-chain - no source dependency-vuln audit exists (no dotnet list --vulnerable, no pnpm audit, no Dependabot config); the image CVE scan blocks only on the release publish job (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~872) while PRs are report-only ~526). Reuse the existing locked/frozen restore + the Trivy gate. Update docs/14, README.

title: Make the line-coverage gate blocking
acceptance_criteria: The coverage gate fails CI below an enforced line-coverage floor (the -ReportOnly flag is removed); the floor is set at or just below the currently-measured production coverage and is documented so it can be ratcheted up, ensuring a new untested handler can actually fail the build.
required_tests: scripts/test-coverage-gate.ps1 still passes; CI proves the gate is now blocking (a report below the floor fails); the floor value is asserted/documented.
