notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (test-net enforcement - the gate exists and is unit-tested but is wired -ReportOnly so it never fails the build: .github/workflows/ci.yml ~124 runs assert-coverage.ps1 with -ReportOnly; assert-coverage.ps1 ~69-72 only warns). Measure current coverage first, set the floor just under it, then drop -ReportOnly. Reuse the existing fail-closed gate logic + production-only exclusions. Update docs/14, docs/17 (Definition of Done), README.

title: Sign and attest the published container images and SBOMs
acceptance_criteria: On a release tag, after the CVE gate passes, each pushed image is signed (keyless OIDC cosign) and its CycloneDX SBOM is attached as an attestation; cosign verify and cosign verify-attestation against the published digest succeed in CI; the id-token write permission is scoped to the publish job only.
required_tests: A publish-pipeline step (mirrored in publish-dry-run against the locally-built digest, no push) runs cosign verify / verify-attestation and fails closed if the signature or SBOM attestation is missing or invalid.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (supply-chain - the publish job builds, scans and pushes images but never produces a signature or verifiable provenance/SBOM attestation; the SBOMs are only actions/upload-artifact build artifacts misleadingly named "supply-chain-attestations" (.github/workflows/ci.yml ~894-903), never cosign sign/attest or --provenance; README.md ~3841 already records cryptographic provenance as a follow-up. So a self-hoster cannot prove a ghcr.io image was built by this pipeline). New dependency: cosign CLI installed the same way Trivy/pg-client already are (or actions/attest-build-provenance). Reuse the release-gated publish job and the existing SBOM. Pairs with CORE-PUB-004. Update .github, docs/14, README.

title: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and add a dependency-update policy
acceptance_criteria: Every uses: in .github/workflows/* is pinned to a full 40-char commit SHA (with a readable version in a trailing comment), a .github/dependabot.yml enables github-actions (and the npm/nuget ecosystems) update PRs, and a CI lint fails closed on any uses: ref that is not a SHA.
required_tests: A pwsh lint (mirroring the existing scripts/* gate plus test pattern) scans the workflows and fails on any non-SHA uses: ref, run on every push/PR; a seeded floating-tag ref fails the lint.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (supply-chain - every third-party action is referenced by a mutable major tag (actions/checkout@v4, setup-dotnet@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-artifact@v4 - .github/workflows/ci.yml ~48/51/114/134/532/895), so a compromised or retagged action runs with the publish job's packages: write token; no .github/dependabot.yml or renovate.json exists. CORE-DEP-005 covers the dependency vuln audit gate, not action pinning or update automation). Extend the digest-pinning discipline the Dockerfiles already apply to base images (apps/api/Dockerfile ~33) to the workflows. No heavyweight tool (Dependabot is GitHub-native). Update .github, docs/14.

title: Ship a Helm chart for the Core runtime
acceptance_criteria: A Helm chart deploys the API and worker with the migrations runner as a pre-install/pre-upgrade Job that must succeed before the API rolls out, externalizes all configuration via ConfigMap/Secret (no baked secrets), wires the documented liveness/readiness probes and a Service/Ingress, and is lint/template-validated in CI; the chart matches the migrate-before-API contract the Compose stack already enforces.
required_tests: CI helm lint + helm template (and/or kubeconform) render the chart and assert the pre-install migrate Job, the probes, and that no secret is hardcoded; the rendered manifests pass schema validation.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (operations - docs/13 ~93/149-151 lists Kubernetes with Helm as a first-class production option but the repo has NO chart/manifest anywhere; only deploy/compose exists, so the K8s story is documentation-only). Mirror the Compose contract (deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml - migrate gate + pg healthcheck + external probes) in a deploy/helm chart. Reuse the same configuration keys (ConnectionStrings__Database, OIDC, S3, CORS). Update docs/13, deploy/, README. Justify any chart tooling in CI.

title: Add a full local stack compose profile with OIDC storage and backplane
acceptance_criteria: An optional Compose profile/overlay brings up the Core together with an OIDC provider (Keycloak), S3-compatible object storage (RustFS or MinIO) and a Redis/Valkey backplane, pre-wired so an operator or vertical author can run the platform end-to-end locally (authenticated traffic, asset upload/download, multi-instance realtime) without standing up external services by hand.
required_tests: scripts/test-compose-deploy.ps1 (or a sibling) statically validates the full-stack profile wires the OIDC/storage/backplane services and that the api/worker reference them; the compose-smoke CI job can bring up the profile (or a documented subset) and the probes answer 200.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (self-hosting/adoption - the shipped minimal stack deliberately omits OIDC, object storage and the backplane (docker-compose.yml defines only postgres/migrate/api/worker), so nobody can run an authenticated, asset-serving, scaled Core locally out of the box). Reuse the documented config contract + the existing migrate gate. Keep it a separate profile so the minimal stack stays minimal. Underpins CORE-PUB-003 (the example needs a real OIDC+API). Update deploy/compose, docs/13, README.

title: Remove the Development-default production footgun
acceptance_criteria: A production deployment cannot accidentally run in the Development posture - ship a production Compose overlay defaulting to ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production with the prod readiness/OIDC gates active, and emit a loud persistent startup warning when the API/worker run in Development while bound to a non-loopback interface, so the green-but-unauthenticated default cannot ship silently.
required_tests: A test asserting the production overlay sets Production; a host test that Development on a non-loopback bind logs the warning; the existing Production fail-closed readiness/OIDC-audience behavior is unchanged.
notes: TIER 2 MEDIUM (operations footgun - deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml ~98/135 and .env.example default ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development, where the readiness gate is inert and the OIDC audience guard does not trip (Hosting/RequiredDependencyReadiness.cs ~49-53, IdentityAccess/OidcAuthenticationExtensions.cs ~109-116), so copying the defaults to a server yields a green but open API). Add a docker-compose.prod.yml overlay + a startup warning; do not weaken the legitimate local-dev default. Reuse the existing environment-aware gates. Update deploy/compose/README.md, docs/13.

title: Lock concurrent migration runners with a PostgreSQL advisory lock
acceptance_criteria: The migration step acquires a session-level pg_advisory_lock on a fixed app key before applying and releases it after, so a second concurrent runner blocks until the first completes and then applies nothing (idempotent, exits 0); two runners launched simultaneously against an empty database both exit 0 with exactly one applied set and a consistent __EFMigrationsHistory.
required_tests: Integration: launch two migrate processes concurrently against one empty PostgreSQL and assert both exit 0, the schema is applied once, and the history table is consistent; assert the second blocks (does not error) until the first releases.
notes: TIER 2 HIGH (deploy-safety - the migrate-before-API gate stops API replicas racing to migrate, but nothing stops two migration-RUNNER invocations racing (a retried Helm pre-upgrade hook, an overlapping redeploy, two operator runs): apps/api/Migrations.Dockerfile ~68-83 just runs efbundle with no lock, and EnableRetryOnFailure (Persistence/LiveCoreNpgsqlOptions.cs ~62-73) can re-issue a half-applied migration; a grep for advisory/pg_advisory returns zero in apps/. Two concurrent runners can both attempt the same Up() and corrupt the schema or the history table). Wrap the apply in a pg advisory lock. Complements CORE-DEP-004 (Helm pre-install Job). Update docs/13.

title: Add container resource limits and capacity/sizing guidance
acceptance_criteria: The compose services declare reasonable default memory/CPU limits (overridable via env), and docs/13 (or the deploy README) documents a minimum/recommended sizing baseline per component (API, worker, Postgres) and a when-to-add-API-replicas/backplane note tied to CORE-OPS-007; the existing scripts/test-compose-deploy.ps1 static validation stays green.
required_tests: scripts/test-compose-deploy.ps1 stays green while asserting each service carries a resource limit; the compose-smoke CI job still brings the stack up and the probes answer 200; a doc review that a sizing baseline table exists.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (self-hosting - deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml ~48-160 defines postgres/migrate/api/worker with no deploy.resources/mem_limit/cpus, and no doc gives memory/CPU/replica sizing (docs/02 and docs/13 have zero capacity content), so an unbounded process can starve a single-VPS host and an operator has no starting point. CORE-RES-004 sizes the DB connection pool, not container CPU/memory; CORE-DEP-004 (Helm) is a separate manifest). Lightweight (compose deploy.resources plus a docs sizing table). Complements CORE-DEP-004, CORE-RES-004. Update deploy/compose, docs/13, README.

title: Validate critical configuration values for well-formedness at startup
acceptance_criteria: At startup the host validates well-formedness of the critical values it can check without I/O (the database connection string parses, Authority is an absolute URI, each Cors:AllowedOrigins entry is scheme+host[+port] with no path/wildcard, each ForwardedHeaders KnownNetworks entry is a parseable CIDR) and emits the same loud named Critical log and not-ready posture for a malformed value as for a missing one - by key name only, never the value.
required_tests: Unit: each malformed value is reported by name and no value is logged; a well-formed set reports nothing. Integration: a Production host with a malformed CORS origin reports not-ready and logs the offending key name only.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability - Hosting/ProductionConfigurationValidator.cs ~83-107 checks only that required keys are non-blank, never that the values parse, so a malformed connection string / Authority / CORS origin / KnownNetworks CIDR is discovered only at first request or silently misbehaves - inconsistent with Hosting/GracefulShutdownConfiguration.cs ~78-92 and the worker options, which reject malformed values loudly at startup. Reuse the existing startup-validation and not-ready posture. Extends CORE-OPS-008/011. Update docs/13.

title: Add a failure-response operations runbook for degraded dependencies and worker backlog
acceptance_criteria: A runbook (in docs/13 or a sibling) maps each readiness/liveness/alert signal to operator actions for the four documented dependencies (database, OIDC, object storage, realtime backplane) and for worker dead-letter/backlog growth, cross-referencing the readiness gate, heartbeat liveness and the CORE-OBS-007/008 metrics; it uses no forbidden vertical term (name it an operations/failure-response runbook).
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green; the boundary scan over the new doc confirms no forbidden term leaks; a manual cross-reference that every dependency in the CORE-OPS-008 contract table has a runbook entry.
notes: TIER 3 MEDIUM (operability; docs only - docs/13 has a tested restore runbook (~1016) and a migration rollback policy (~207) but no consolidated runbook for degraded-state response; CORE-OBS-008 ships alert rules/SLOs/dashboards (what to alert on) but explicitly not response procedures, and CORE-RES-002 adds a dead-letter state/metric but no drain runbook, so the operator has signals without a playbook). Mirror the docs/24 / docs/13 runbook style; no new infra. CAUTION: the vertical term for an unplanned-disruption event is forbidden (csv/forbidden_core_terms.csv) - word it as failure-response. Complements CORE-OBS-007/008, CORE-RES-002. Update docs/13.

title: Reconcile the architecture docs with the shipped package reality
acceptance_criteria: The docs no longer overstate the package surface - docs/02 is corrected (or annotated with a dated decision) so the ui-core description matches its framework-agnostic prop-contract reality (it ships typed prop/variant contracts and the vertical owns rendering - it is NOT a React component library) and the contracts description matches reality until CORE-OAS-002 makes OpenAPI-derived true; the deliberate design is recorded so a reader can tell an intentional boundary from a gap; the doc/csv consistency checks stay green.
required_tests: Doc/CSV consistency stays green (the CORE-SPEC-001 checks); no Core source change.
notes: TIER 3 LOW (hygiene; docs only - docs/02 ~72 claims OpenAPI-derived contracts and ~78 claims ui-core ships React components, but contracts are hand-written (until CORE-OAS-002) and packages/ui-core/src/index.ts + props.ts ship only interfaces/variant defaults with no react dependency, consistent with the docs/04 vertical-owns-rendering boundary). Mirror the CORE-SPEC-003 decision-register style in docs/24. Decide explicitly whether a thin reference component kit is ever in scope (Core-later vs vertical) and record it. No endpoints. Pairs with CORE-OAS-001/002 and CORE-PUB-003.

title: Track and replace the prerelease Prometheus exporter
acceptance_criteria: The Prometheus metrics exporter dependency is either upgraded to a stable release once one exists or its prerelease use is recorded as an explicit dated owner-named decision with the upgrade trigger, so the /metrics dependency is not silently riding a beta; the metrics endpoint behavior is unchanged.
required_tests: The metrics endpoint integration test stays green; a dependency assertion/comment records the pinned version and the upgrade trigger.
notes: TIER 3 LOW (operations/supply-chain - apps/api/LiveCore.Api.csproj ~76 pins OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Prometheus.AspNetCore 1.16.0-beta.1 and the csproj comments acknowledge no stable release exists). If no stable release yet, record the decision (mirror the docs/24 deferral style) rather than churn. Reuse the existing metrics wiring (MetricsServiceCollectionExtensions.cs). Update docs/15, docs/24.
